title: Interval Problems Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision of the interval problem family: sort-then-scan merging, insertion, overlap tests, meeting rooms via min-heap, sweep line events, and greedy removal by end time.

chapters.title: Intervals: Overlap and Sort-First Mental Model
points: Interval = [start, end]; two intervals a, b overlap iff a.start <= b.end AND b.start <= a.end
After sorting by start, you only compare each interval with the previous one (or running end), never all pairs
Touching endpoints ([1,2],[2,3]): merge problems treat as overlap (<=); meeting-room problems treat as no overlap (<) - read the statement
Sort cost O(n log n) dominates; the scan after sorting is O(n)
Pick the key by goal: sort by start to merge/insert/count rooms, sort by end to maximize kept intervals

chapters.title: Merge Intervals and Insert Interval
points: Merge: sort by start, keep result list; if cur.start <= last.end then last.end = max(last.end, cur.end) else append cur
Use max(last.end, cur.end) not cur.end - a fully contained interval must not shrink the end
Insert (input already sorted, O(n)): add all intervals ending before new.start; merge all that overlap by min of starts and max of ends; add the rest
Insert loop condition for overlap: interval.start <= new.end, and the left phase uses interval.end < new.start
Common bug: sorting the input in place when the caller expects the original order, or mutating the last list element's alias

chapters.title: Meeting Rooms with a Min-Heap
points: Meeting Rooms I: sort by start, return false if any intervals[i].start < intervals[i-1].end
Meeting Rooms II: sort by start; min-heap holds end times of rooms currently in use; heap size = rooms needed
For each meeting: if heap top <= meeting.start, pop (room freed); then push meeting.end; answer = max heap size seen
Use <= for the pop so a meeting starting exactly when another ends reuses the room
Complexity O(n log n) time, O(n) space; forgetting to sort first or heapifying starts instead of ends gives wrong counts

chapters.title: Sweep Line with Events
points: Turn each interval into events: (start, +1) and (end, -1); sort events by time; running sum = concurrent intervals
Tie-break at equal time: process -1 before +1 when touching ends should not overlap; reverse if touching counts as overlap
Answer = max running sum (meeting rooms, max concurrent users); also returns the time of the peak
Alternative with two sorted arrays: starts[] and ends[], two pointers; if start < end advance start and count++, else advance end and count--
Sweep beats heap on simplicity and extends to weights (+w/-w) and coordinate-compressed or difference-array problems; same O(n log n)

chapters.title: Non-Overlapping Intervals by End Time
points: Goal: minimum removals so the rest do not overlap = n - maximum kept intervals
Greedy: sort by END ascending; keep an interval if start >= lastEnd (then lastEnd = its end), else count a removal
Earliest finish leaves the most room for later intervals; sorting by start fails on [[1,100],[2,3],[3,4]] by keeping the long one
Same greedy solves activity selection and minimum arrows to burst balloons (touching counts as overlap there, so use <= or adjust the compare)
Alternative by start: on overlap, drop the interval with the larger end and keep the smaller as lastEnd
Complexity O(n log n) time, O(1) extra space; initialize lastEnd to -infinity, not 0, when starts can be negative

chapters.title: Intervals Cheat Sheet
points: Overlap test: a.start <= b.end and b.start <= a.end (use < when touching is allowed)
Merge: sort by start, extend last.end = max(last.end, cur.end) when cur.start <= last.end
Insert: three phases - before, merge overlapping, after; O(n) on sorted input
Meeting rooms: sort by start + min-heap of end times (pop if top <= start), or sweep line +1/-1 events; answer = peak
Min removals: sort by end, keep if start >= lastEnd, removals = n - kept
Pick key: start for merge/insert/rooms, end for max-keep greedy; always decide touching-endpoint rule first
Complexity: O(n log n) sort-dominated, O(n) for insert on sorted input
